gir_001: You can recognise it by its height, 38.5 metres, extraordinary for a sessile oak, with a crown 26.5 metres across. It stands above Osor, about 480 metres from the great pine.
gir_002: You can recognise it by its trunk, 9.70 metres round, the thickest tree anywhere near Girona, on a crown only 18 metres tall. It stands behind the hermitage on the Pla de Sant Nicolau.
gir_003: You can recognise it by its short, massive pollarded trunk carrying a crown that is entirely regrowth, 5.90 metres round. It stands at L'Aulet, Vidreres.
gir_004: You can recognise it by its narrow, upright shape, 30.5 metres tall, unlike the flat umbrella crown a stone pine usually spreads. It stands south of Romanya de la Selva.
gir_005: You can recognise it by being a shrub species grown to tree size, 5.5 metres tall with a trunk 1.90 metres round. It stands beside the C-255 and GI-652 junction, Torrent.
gir_006: You can recognise it by its smooth, cinnamon-red bark peeling in strips, and in autumn by white flowers and red fruit together. It stands on the track near Can Genoer.
gir_007: You can recognise it by its height, 29 metres, unusual for a pine subspecies that normally favours dry limestone further west. It stands at L'Espinau, Osor.
